issues.title: fix(formula): handle recursive lambdas and Excel array semantics
issues.body:
<!--
 Thank you for submitting a Pull Request.
 Please read our Pull Request guidelines:
 https://github.com/dream-num/univer/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#submitting-pull-requests
-->

No linked issue.

<!-- A description of the proposed changes. -->
## Summary

Recalculating a workbook with recursive named LAMBDAs could overflow during AST expansion. A malformed INDIRECT union could also expand into an enormous reference. These failures prevented the formula supersample from completing calculation.

- Defer recursive named LAMBDA calls, isolate call bindings and cached ASTs, and bound active calls at 64. Excessive recursion returns a cell `#NUM!`; async calls release their call depth after completion.
- Reject malformed/out-of-bounds INDIRECT references and preserve quoted separators and escaped quotes in array constants.
- Correct existing function behavior: omitted defaults in CEILING.MATH/FLOOR.MATH/LINEST/LOGEST; typed UNIQUE identity; BASE/MAKEARRAY/ARRAYTOTEXT validation; value arrays in FACTDOUBLE/MROUND/QUOTIENT/SQRTPI; and array indices in CHOOSECOLS/CHOOSEROWS.
- Retain imported one-cell legacy array-formula context so IF evaluates consistently through the OSS and Pro calculation services. Reject multi-cell references separately from value arrays, while preserving missing-sheet `#REF!` errors.

No missing functions are added. The recursion limit is a protective engine boundary and can reject terminating formulas that exceed it; it is not a promise to match every Excel version's limit. Pro uses this shared core, so no Pro-only source change is required.

<!-- How to test them. -->
## Validation

- Full formula suite: 574 files passed; 4,861 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- Formula package typecheck and ESLint: passed (0 errors; existing lint warnings remain).
- Parser regressions use real services resolved through DI and cover direct/mutual recursion, repeated calls, dirty defined names, async lifecycle, invalid references, quoted arrays, defaults and value/reference distinctions.
- Independent review found a missing-sheet error-precedence regression; fixed with 8 additional DI cases. Parser suite: 157 passed.
- The original workbook was compared through real OSS and Pro calculation services. These are local source checks, not validation of a newly published package combination.

## Excel reference limits

The original workbook's caches were independently recalculated in Excel for Mac 16.87: 16,146 exact value/type matches, with only 30 random/time/CELL-context changes. These caches are not a Windows COM oracle. Platform/version-specific errors, unsupported functions and remaining calculation differences still require separate triage. Full Excel equivalence is not claimed; Windows verification is pending.

## Documentation

Documented the 64-call named LAMBDA safety boundary and its difference from Excel-version recursion limits in the formula package's Integration Notes.

## Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Related tickets or issues have been linked in the PR description (or missing issue).
- [x] [Naming convention](https://github.com/dream-num/univer/blob/dev/docs/NAMING_CONVENTION.md) is followed (**do please** check it especially when you created new plugins, commands and resources).
- [x] Unit tests have been added for the changes (if applicable).
- [x] Breaking changes have been documented (or no breaking changes introduced in this PR).

issues.title: [Bug] Stale calculation result is written into a cell whose reference formula was just replaced
issues.body:
## Affected packages and versions

`@univerjs/engine-formula` 1.4.0 (also present on `dev` at 54427614f3, 2026-11-12), with `@univerjs/sheets` 1.4.0.

## Summary

`SetRangeValuesMutation` rejects a formula result when the cell's formula no longer matches the formula the result was computed from (`isStaleFormulaResult`, using `sourceFormulaData`). That check never runs for results that are references or arrays, because `FormulaRuntimeService.setRuntimeData` does not record a source formula on those paths:

- **Single-cell reference** (`=$B$4`, `=A5`): the branch commented "If the referenced range or array only contains a single value, such as A5…" writes `sheetData` and returns without touching `_sourceFormulaData` (`packages/engine-formula/src/services/runtime.service.ts`, around line 758 on `dev`).
- **Multi-cell reference / array** (`=B5:B6`, `=SEQUENCE(1,2,50)`): the array branch writes the anchor and spill cells and also records no source.

Only the scalar branch (around line 894) and `preserveCurrentCellData` record it.

Because a running calculation is cancelled only when the debounced trigger fires (about 10 ms after the dirtying command), there is a window in which a calculation that has already built its tree list resumes after a cell's formula was replaced. For a scalar formula the stale result is rejected. For a reference or array formula it is applied.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Workbook with `B4 = 50`, `C4 = "=$B$4"`.
2. Start a calculation that includes C4 (any edit that dirties it) and let `FormulaDependencyGenerator.generate()` return.
3. Before the calculation's first macrotask yield resumes, execute `SetRangeValuesCommand` on C4 with `{ v: null, f: null }`.
4. Let the calculation finish.

Deterministic harness we used: wrap `IFormulaDependencyGenerator.generate` so that, once its result contains the C4 tree, it awaits a promise that is resolved right after step 3's command returns.

Spill variant: `B5 = 0.25`, `B6 = 50`, write `C7 = "=B5:B6"`, then clear C7 in the same window.

(No hosted reproduction link yet; happy to provide a failing unit test.)

## Expected behavior

The stale result is dropped, as it is for a scalar formula such as `=SUM(...)`: C4 stays empty. In the spill variant C7 and C8 stay empty.

## Actual behavior

C4 has no formula and holds the plain value `50`. The value is in the saved snapshot. In the spill variant C7 holds `0.25` and C8 holds `50` as plain values.

The calculation result's `sourceFormulaData` contains entries for scalar formulas in the same run (for example a `=SUM(C2:C4)` total) but none for the reference cells.

## Suggested fix

Record the source formula on the single-value branch the same way the scalar branch does:

```ts
sheetData.setValue(row, column, valueObject);
if (this._currentSourceFormula != null) {
    const unitFormulas = this._sourceFormulaData[unitId] ??= {};
    const sheetFormulas = unitFormulas[sheetId] ??= {};
    const rowFormulas = sheetFormulas[row] ??= {};
    rowFormulas[column] = { ...this._currentSourceFormula };
}
clearArrayUnitData.setValue(row, column, valueObject);
```

We verified this for single-cell references: the reproduction above fails without it and passes with it, and fresh results were not rejected after value edits, a row insert, identical re-entry, undo, a shared formula, a cross-sheet reference or a defined name.

The array branch needs the same for the anchor cell, plus an equivalent check where array results are applied (`SetArrayFormulaDataMutation`); we have not written or tested that part.

## System information

Reproduced in Node (jsdom) unit tests on macOS and Linux; not browser specific.

issues.title: feat(docs): support editable references and Word layout metadata
issues.body:
<!-- A description of the proposed changes. -->
## Description

Release unit-scoped undo/redo state when documents are disposed, and retain Word fallback indentation for nested TOC entries when named styles are missing. Other active units and authored TOC styles remain authoritative.

Preserve complete newly inserted field metadata through grouped bookmark/insertion/refresh composition, and retain section-only formatting during composition. Existing static Core cases verify association, inverse restoration and peer convergence.

Add document model, editing and layout support for editable DOCX references. Fields, bookmarks, bibliography metadata and note segments retain their identities through rich-text edits and undo. Rendering resolves imported Word paragraph, font and table properties, repeated story fields and nested reference results through the existing synchronous and incremental Docs layout paths.

Traditional documents expose reference authoring controls. Modern documents hide the TOC/reference UI while retaining imported fields and cached results. Bookmark targets retain the text cursor; hyperlinks and note anchors retain navigation cursors. Page labels follow Univer's actual pagination.

Concurrent inline and paragraph input at a paragraph boundary now retains the same paragraph identities on both peers. Serialize the existing TextX identity marker so replay cannot reinterpret a boundary insertion as an interior split; the marker is not persisted in the document body.

The added reference tests create models and render objects through DI. Service subjects are registered and resolved with real providers, and fixtures dispose their owned runtimes. Layout calculations are split into row-fragment sizing, whitespace-line reflow and overflow measurement without changing their arithmetic or ordering. The three CodeFactor findings are fixed.

Companion authoring/Ribbon: https://github.com/dream-num/univer-pro/pull/6089. DOCX exchange: https://github.com/dream-num/univer-rs/pull/406. Archived Word controls: https://github.com/dream-num/univer-e2e/pull/61. No public issue is linked.

## Compatibility and integration

The public core document model owns the editable reference and Word compatibility data. Exchange reads and writes it; Docs and the reference plugin edit and render it. Existing snapshots remain readable, but newly imported compatibility settings can change font fallback, spacing, note placement and field fitting. SDK/native artifacts must be coordinated before promotion.

Keep the existing root/worker exports and shared UI/design architecture. No binary artifacts, sibling-checkout dependencies or submodule gitlink changes are submitted. Document protection/revision coupling and global photo resampling remain outside the agreed scope.

Pending JSONX operations now retain their original values after later header/footer/note edits; only operation payloads are cloned, rather than whole documents. Imported nonempty legacy section IDs are preserved. RichTextEditingMutation gains a transient skipHistory option for manually owned history while retaining collaboration; the existing noHistory/IME behavior is unchanged, with no stored-document or wire-format field added. Worker table hydration preserves source identity for unchanged resolved grids, and drawing print visibility is independent of interactive culling.

<!-- How to test them. -->
## Validation

Traditional Docs expose References authoring; Modern hides authoring UI and preserves compatible data/APIs. Page references use each renderer's actual pagination. Formula/LaTeX collaboration, protection/revision coupling (11 corpus controls), global photo resampling and whole-document Word pagination parity are excluded by agreement.

- Current heads: OSS `03926bf69d452ddd0ec6c6f13639935d4e88d8b3` on `dev@0d7923dd7`; Pro `73eee0cf34c51cc2bb39522f92cd97b9035e3281` on `dev@67bc10e4a`; native `37050150c54b46f40db095cdb4b09dcd2b0ec563` on `main@6912013`; E2E `35429c2c1a3b30e12ed6ae11179ae23ab8a9c9ba` on `main@9a10f2dd`. No feature submodule gitlink is submitted. Maintainer milestone assignments are retained. The native rebase changes release metadata/changelog only; all reference codec production/test source files are byte-identical to the previously verified native head.
- Latest fixes: the shared OSS TOC builder retains UI preset numbering, custom list overrides, local number fonts, marked-character offsets, Word tab-switch behavior and section-column widths. Initial insertion and legacy update use it; Pro supplies entry metadata without duplicate formatting. Synchronous/already-completed pagination no longer waits for a missing progress event. Automatic directory bookmarks now use the existing range successor hint, preserving complete snapshots during concurrent input. No new stored-document field, server registration or collaboration protocol is introduced.
- Local verification: **4,123 reference tests pass / 5 existing skips**, **62 TOC tests pass**; owned typechecks and lint pass (existing warnings retained). Review findings have been resolved, with **zero unresolved GitHub inline review threads**. Newly added convergence tests reproduce both delivery priorities with multiple automatic bookmarks. Managed test subjects use DI. Earlier unchanged-path evidence includes 561 Core, 4,200 Docs render, 22 reference UI and 18 print tests. Post-release-rebase native DOCX unit rerun: **633/633 pass**.
- Original DOCX native import/export corpus: **200/200**; browser-updated native export/reimport independent audit: **200/200**. Word print controls: original **200/200**, exported **200/200**, all read-only with source digests. Native binary identity remains explicitly pinned to the tested Traditional build; subsequent native production changes affect Modern hyphenation only.
- Immutable browser baseline: normal exit **true**, independent acceptance **200/200**, **13034** own-pagination checks, repeated refresh idempotent for all 200, no page errors/crash. Raw 102 expects decimal 1 instead of the correct restarted Roman i; its original raw failure is retained. An identity correction records that this baseline compiled Pro `d000b98cd` with linked OSS `c2eeab1bbc`, not the separate outer OSS checkout.
- Follow-up evidence is versioned separately: the Pro `878fb6f99` / OSS `82a026aaf` browser/print cohort passes **32/32**, native **32/32**, covering all 11 detected note-continuation layouts. Pro `259fa2b7b` / OSS `daaa389289` adds fresh 092/104/192 browser **3/3** and native **3/3** controls. Native OOXML independently verifies repaired/preserved TOC tabs before Word refresh.
- Identical-input full-corpus differentials: numbered-tab repair **200/200** (only tab formatting changes); preset support **200/200**; shared builder **200/200**; final bookmark-positioning code **200/200**, complete **true**. Actual saved models/pages are identical inputs; these are evaluator comparisons, not fresh 200-document screenshots on the final head.
- Latest selected-build real-gateway regression: **6/6 pass**, **0 unexpected**; Traditional/Modern × Main/Worker plus numbered-directory Main/Worker. Scenarios require initial numbering/tab, one undo/redo, successful legacy update with numbering/tab retained, concurrent repair/input, exact complete peer snapshots, empty queues, repeated-refresh stability and persisted reload. Worker cases assert actual Worker activation. Actual served URLs/assets are recorded for every final case. Earlier local-adapter attempts dropped the build subpath and reached the older frozen build; those raw failures are retained, not attributed to the final product head. Earlier 16-scenario gateway evidence is retained under its own build identity.
- Supplemental Word note-page audit: **64/64**, including **6 manual page resolutions** for source-empty endnotes; six viewed Word/Univer pairs, input XML and PDF/raster hashes support those resolutions. Additional controls, including late case 192, pass **12/12**. Raw failed automatic text matching is retained. Empty-note manual page resolution does not certify full pixel parity.
- Display triage maps **4424 fields / 200 documents**, zero unmatched; exported triage maps **4424 / 200**, zero unmatched. The two remaining inline-picture placeholders are independently checked for original binary data, size and geometry. Original/export galleries contain **200 pairs each**. The visual ledger records **29 original full-page reviews**, with note-page review recorded separately.
- E2E registry: **1,267 tests / 103 files**, including **164 collaboration cases**; **23 tooling** and **567 contract** checks, typecheck, focused lint and owned formatting pass. Counts describe registration, not execution of every browser case. Root CLI check has 293 existing formatting failures; E2E full check has 22 untouched formatting failures. User edits are retained.

## Remaining acceptance

- **P1 — Full visual acceptance remains open.** All 400 original/export full-page pairs are generated, but every reference region has not been reviewed. Data/text checks and evaluator equivalence do not certify whole-page pixel equality or every page of a long file. The automated corpus/follow-up gate is **complete**.
- **P2 — Visible presentation differences:** title shading (005/016), German hyphenation (010), TOC row pitch (028), address-block flow (101), side-watermark rotation (141), footer alignment (036), and vertical note placement (067). Their baseline/origin is not established; no whole-page/no-regression claim is made. Control 009's font substitution is attributable to an Office private-cloud font unavailable to the browser; a local FontFace control fixes it without distributing the font.
- **P2 — Interoperability:** 104's English STYLEREF Title instruction fails in Chinese Word; a localized read-only control resolves the same title. Original instructions are preserved. Native chart metadata round-trips do not certify Pro chart rendering parity.
- **P2 — Minor directory formatting normalization:** the legacy authoring path can place a right page-number tab at 650px, while the first whole reference refresh applies Word's 10-twip inset at 649.333px. The new targeted repair scenario checks the exact left number tab it removes; it does not assert that the legacy right-tab position survives Word normalization. Complete peer snapshots are still compared exactly.
- **P2 — CI/performance evidence:** Draft OSS/Pro jobs are skipped, so full remote CI is not claimed green; current security scans pass. [Native pre-rebase CI](https://github.com/dream-num/univer-rs/actions/runs/43569918434) and [three-platform license contracts](https://github.com/dream-num/univer-rs/actions/runs/43569918257) pass; new-head CI after the release-only rebase is tracked separately. [Forced full native CI](https://github.com/dream-num/univer-rs/actions/runs/43569914898) fails finance_sample.xlsx; [main reproduces the same failure](https://github.com/dream-num/univer-rs/actions/runs/43565498187) with identical diff digest. No golden/gate is weakened. No matched long-document performance baseline or full cross-browser certification is claimed. Pro retains a historical changes-requested decision and needs maintainer re-review.

## Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Related tickets or issues have been linked in the PR description (companion PRs linked; no public issue provided).
- [x] [Naming convention](https://github.com/dream-num/univer/blob/dev/docs/NAMING_CONVENTION.md) is followed.
- [x] Unit tests have been added for the changes; managed subjects/providers use DI.
- [x] Breaking changes and compatibility limits have been documented.
